headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-flow confusion: Perplexity can ingest web content, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot act, so most pairwise harms are blocked or low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can browse the web and analyze uploaded documents, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no execution or input channel, so there is no direct automated bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or user-mediated transfer, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Perplexity output into another prompt or document
IF attacker-controlled text is uploaded to Perplexity and then reused verbatim
mitigations: Avoid copying raw web excerpts into downstream prompts
Add a human review step before reuse of Perplexity output
Strip instructions from pasted content
Use quoted blocks for source text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context, but its network egress is vendor-only. python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces. There is no shared workspace or authenticated channel in the profiles, so leakage between the pair is limited to user-mediated copying rather than automatic exposure.
conditions: IF the operator pastes sensitive Perplexity output into python-cheatsheet-related artifacts
IF uploaded documents contain secrets and are summarized externally
mitigations: Do not paste sensitive excerpts into downstream docs
Redact secrets before reuse
Keep Perplexity sessions separate by topic
Review sharing settings before uploading files
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on copied text

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity has no filesystem write, no git modification, and no shell execution; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-runnable. With no overlapping mutable resource or write surface, there is no plausible capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF either profile is changed to gain write access to the same directory
IF an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only
Do not mount a shared writable workspace
Avoid granting git or filesystem write scopes
Document any future shared-state integration
requires-engineering: add locking if write access is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity can produce cited answers, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot take downstream actions or autonomously trust inputs. That makes cascading error mostly a manual reuse problem, not an automated chain. The pair lacks an action-taking second agent, so the blast radius stays small.
conditions: IF a human treats Perplexity output as authoritative and republishes it into the cheatsheet
IF the cheatsheet content is manually edited based on unverified Perplexity claims
mitigations: Verify claims against primary sources
Mark generated text as untrusted until checked
Use a second reviewer for factual edits
Keep source links alongside copied text
requires-engineering: add citation validation in the publishing workflow

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context under vendor-hosted service terms, while python-cheatsheet is open-source documentation-only and touches no data classes. The pair does not show a residency or certification mismatch in the profiles, but any sensitive upload to Perplexity could create a policy issue if reused in documentation.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to Perplexity and then copied into public documentation
IF an organization requires local-only handling for the same content
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data without approval
Remove personal data before analysis
Keep public docs free of sensitive excerpts
Check organizational retention rules
requires-engineering: add a compliance gate before upload
